The HEDS, which can be implemented in either CAV or VAV systems, was created to help the Department of Defense solve HVAC-related problems such as poor indoor air quality (IAQ), poor environmental control, excessive electrical & fossil fuel energy use, biological growth and corrosion. The HEDS technology includes two high performance counter-flow heat exchanger coils to dehumidify air and subsequently recover much of the low-quality heat generated in the cooling and dehumidification process, reducing the load on the chiller while simultaneously limiting the need for reheat of the air. The HEDS also uses advanced HVAC system optimization control strategies designed to minimize energy waste that is common in many legacy systems that operate the cooling coil to maintain a fixed supply air dry bulb temperature setpoint. The dehumidification and heat recovery coils combined with the optimized controls result in precise and efficient humidity and temperature control that automatically responds to changes in ambient temperature, humidity, occupancy and other operating conditions to minimize energy use while maintaining occupant comfort. iv This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. The HEDS was one of three technologies selected to be part of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) High Impact Technology Catalyst (HIT) evaluation program in 2022. The U.S. General Services Administration Green Proving Ground (GSA-GPG) and DOE-HIT programs are designed to help identify, prioritize, and deploy cost effective and innovative energy efficiency solutions that can provide significant cost savings to businesses while leading market transformation through deployment of new American-made building technologies. Demonstrations were conducted to collect real building performance data and quantify the savings potential of selected technologies with an end goal to accelerate implementation and market acceptance of promising energy saving technologies. At the request of the Department of Energy, HEDS was field tested by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL). NREL completed an analysis of data collected at the Timken Museum to assess the system performance of the HEDS energy recovery, energy efficiency, and building electrification technology. Evaluations were conducted in summer 2023 (August 1- September 11, 2023), winter 2024 (December 27, 2023-February 6, 2024) and spring 2024 (May 14-June 11, 2024) to characterize and compare the HEDS performance under various seasonal operating conditions. The HVAC system was operated with and without the cooling recovery coil and optimized HEDS controls in both CAV and VAV operating modes to allow comparisons representative of conventional CAV and VAV operation.
